_comment: TEMPLATE — copy this file to testset.json and replace every field below with real questions against a real PDF. JSON has no comment syntax, so this key is just documentation and is ignored by scripts/benchmark.py.

_fields.pdf: Path to the PDF the questions below are asked against. Overridable per run with --pdf.
_fields.cases[].id: Short unique id, used in the raw CSV and the failure-analysis log.
_fields.cases[].question: The question asked to the pipeline, verbatim.
_fields.cases[].expected_answer_contains: Phrases a CORRECT answer must contain. This list is doing double duty: (1) it scores the final answer (match_mode below decides any/all), and (2) it is the objective oracle used to check whether a given round's retrieved context actually held the answer, independent of what the grader said about it. Keep phrases short and load-bearing (a number, a name, a specific term) — not full sentences — so substring matching is meaningful.
_fields.cases[].match_mode: 'any' (default) or 'all' — whether one matching phrase is enough or all of them must appear.
_fields.cases[].notes: Optional. Free text for your own reference.

cases.question: REPLACE ME — a specific, narrow question the PDF can answer.
expected_answer_contains: REPLACE ME — a short exact phrase from the correct answer
cases.notes: TEMPLATE row — delete once you have real cases.

cases.question: REPLACE ME — a broad question the PDF likely cannot fully answer (used to test whether the grader correctly keeps rejecting it).
cases.notes: TEMPLATE row — include a few cases you expect to fail even at round 3, so the accuracy table isn't just easy questions.
